```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(numbers)
n = 4
while(T){
    p = sample(c(2,3,4,5,6),n,T)
    q = sample(c(2,3,5,6,7,10),n,T)
    negs = sample(c(-1,1),n,T)
    handles = paste0(p,"#",q)
    if(length(unique(handles))==n && abs(diff(c(sum(negs==1),sum(negs==-1))))<=1 && negs[1]==-1){break}
}

qstr = paste0("* $\\sqrt{",negs*p^2*q,"}=$ ##ANSWER",1:n,"##",collapse="\n")
astr1= paste0("$",p,"\\sqrt{",q,"}$")
astr2= paste0("$",p,"i\\sqrt{",q,"}$")
astr3= paste0("$",q,"\\sqrt{",p,"}$")
astr4= paste0("$",q,"i\\sqrt{",p,"}$")
ach = sort(unique(c(astr1,astr2,astr3,astr4)))

al = paste0("* ",ach,collapse="\n")

pp = p[1]
qq = q[1]
nn = -1

sol = paste0(1*(ach==paste0("$",pp,"i\\sqrt{",qq,"}$")),collapse="")

```

Question
========

Simplify the following radical expression.

$$\sqrt{`r -pp^2*qq`}$$


Answerlist
--------

`r al`


Solution
========


$$\sqrt{`r -pp^2*qq`}$$

Use [prime factorization](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_factorization).

$$\sqrt{(-1)\cdot `r paste0(primeFactors(pp^2*qq),collapse="\\cdot")`}$$

Isolate twins.

$$\sqrt{`r paste0(primeFactors(pp^2),collapse="\\cdot")`\cdot (-1)\cdot `r paste0(primeFactors(qq),collapse="\\cdot")`}$$


$$\sqrt{`r pp^2`}\cdot \sqrt{-1}\cdot \sqrt{`r qq`}$$

$$`r pp`i \sqrt{`r qq`}$$
